[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Batch Processing vs Stream Processing in ETL Architectures"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern data engineering relies heavily on moving and transforming data from sources to destinations. When designing an Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipeline, choosing the right data processing paradigm is crucial. The two primary paradigms are Batch Processing and Stream Processing."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Batch Processing"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Batch processing involves collecting data over a specific period and processing it all at once as a single batch. This approach is ideal for large volumes of data where immediate insights are not required."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"High throughput: Efficiently processes massive datasets by utilizing parallel computing."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cost-effective: Often scheduled during off-peak hours to optimize resource utilization."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"High latency: Results are only available after the entire batch finishes running."},{"order":8,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Stream Processing"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Stream processing, or real-time processing, handles data records individually or in micro-batches as soon as they are generated. This paradigm is critical for use cases requiring immediate analytics and rapid response times."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Low latency: Data is processed in milliseconds or seconds, enabling real-time dashboards."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Continuous ingestion: Seamlessly handles unbounded data sources like clickstreams or IoT sensors."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Complexity: Requires sophisticated state management and fault-tolerance mechanisms."},{"order":13,"type":"heading","text":"Practical Implementation Examples"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below are conceptual code examples demonstrating how both paradigms are implemented in modern data stacks."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Batch ETL Example (Apache Spark)"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("BatchETL").getOrCreate()

# Extract
df = spark.read.parquet("s3://my-bucket/raw-data/")

# Transform
transformed_df = df.filter(df["status"] == "ACTIVE").groupBy("country").count()

# Load
transformed_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("s3://my-bucket/processed-data/")"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Stream ETL Example (Apache Spark Structured Streaming)"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("StreamETL").getOrCreate()

# Extract (Stream)
streaming_df = spark.readStream.format("kafka") \
    .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
    .option("subscribe", "user-clicks") \
    .load()

# Transform
parsed_df = streaming_df.selectExpr("CAST(value AS STRING) as click_data")

# Load (Stream Sink)
query = parsed_df.writeStream \
    .format("console") \
    .outputMode("append") \
    .start()

query.awaitTermination()"},{"order":19,"type":"heading","text":"Choosing the Right Approach"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"When architecting your ETL pipeline, evaluate your business requirements. Use batch processing for end-of-day financial reports, historical data migrations, and complex aggregations. Use stream processing for fraud detection, real-time recommendations, and live monitoring systems. Often, modern architectures adopt a Lambda or Kappa architecture to combine the strengths of both worlds."}]
